liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mission In The Rain** (2 reviews): Mission in the Rain is described as beyond description; First-set Mission in the Rain is cited as a strong, moving ballad [15][16]
- **Comes A Time** (2 reviews): Jerry's guitar playing on Comes a Time is called dreamlike; the Let It Grow, Wharf Rat, Comes a Time sequence is highlighted; Reviewer calls this one of the worst Comes a Times, blaming Donna's vocals; also says High Time suffers [14][17]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer says the Let It Grow alone justifies the download [19]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat into Comes a Time is highlighted as a Jerry ballad peak, tear-inducing [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mission In The Rain**: rare: 5 archived performances [23]
- **Closing Remarks**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-06-12.132933.mtx.nicksmix.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 190 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: FM source has a brief cut during Mission in the Rain; both sources have cuts between songs [1]
- **gd1976-06-12.143169.fm.warburton.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 24 songs; 188 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd76-06-12.fm.wren.5556.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 186 min; rated 4.48/5 by 42 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the recording as crisp, with plenty of energy across the rest of the show; Reviewer finds the 1976 sound ethereal, linking it to Jerry's guitar tones that year; Reviewer says sound quality for all four Boston shows is excellent [13][14][20]
- **gd1976-06-12.143168.fm.warburton.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 24 songs; 188 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer suggests the band was waiting for the radio broadcast to unleash their best [15]
- Radio announcements are by Norm Winer, called Old Saxophone Joe [1]
- Reviewer says earlier shows in the Boston run build toward this one, and group harmonies are unusually sweet [15]
- Reviewer finds this one of the mellower sets they have heard, calling it a 1976 classic [19]
- One of four Boston shows on consecutive nights, with Music Never Stopped played all four nights [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-06-12.132933.mtx.nicksmix.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Nick Crump; source: Matrix Mix of Shnid 100328 (FM) and Shnid 110456 (AUD) [1]. Also: Matrix mix of FM broadcast and audience sources, roughly 50/50; The Wheel comes from audience tape only [1]
- **gd1976-06-12.143169.fm.warburton.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: FM Broadcast; Master Reel to Reel > Jim Warburton's 1st generation 7" reels @ 3 3/4 ips [2]. Also: Pitch correction was assisted by Joe B. Jones; Warburton's microphones included an AKG D1000E up front [2]
- **gd76-06-12.fm.wren.5556.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - FM [8]
- **gd1976-06-12.143168.fm.warburton.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: FM Broadcast; Master Reel to Reel > Jim Warburton's 1st generation 7" reels @ 3 3/4 ips [3]
